scope: Theorem 7.2 (Joint bilinear principal values) of the manuscript “The maximal triangular Hilbert transform at the symmetric point” (preprints/The-maximal-triangular-Hilbert-transform-at-the-symmetric-point-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 082 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9dbcf9cb984bcf7b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For all complex F, G ∈ L3(ℝ2), the joint limit B(F, G) = lim ε↓0 R↑∞ Bε,R(F, G) exists almost everywhere and in L3/2(ℝ2), with ∥B(F, G)∥3/2 ≤ CM ∥F∥3∥G∥3. More precisely, ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ sup 0<ε<1/n R>n |Bε,R(F, G) − B(F, G)| ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ 3/2 −→ 0. (7.3) The limit is the unique bounded bilinear extension of the principal-value operator on compactly supported smooth inputs.
